key_insight: PSDesigner reproduces a human-like creative workflow to automatically convert user intent into layered, editable design files—giving generative models the flexibility and editability of traditional design tools.
problem_solved: Existing automated design tools produce single-shot, non-editable images or oversimplify professional workflows; PSDesigner addresses the gap between user intent and practical, editable design outputs that support iteration and fine-grained control.
method: Intent understanding and planning: parse natural-language briefs with an MLLM-style planner that produces a multi-step creative plan (assets, layout, style, constraints).
Asset generation and assembly: use generative image/asset models plus vectorization and constraint-aware layout composition to create layered elements.
Iterative refinement into editable files: assemble outputs into standard layered design formats and support looped edits to emulate a human designer's revision workflow.
impact: Makes generative design systems practical for real-world creative workflows by producing editable, revision-friendly outputs—lowering friction for designers and enabling integration of AI into production pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: from user brief → planner → asset generator → layered file output (shows iterative loop for refinements).
Before/after examples: short prompt and resulting flat image vs layered editable file with selectable elements.
UI mockup: mock user interface showing plan steps, style controls, and an edit loop (drag/drop layer, regenerate asset).
Comparison chart: flexibility/editability vs prior text-to-image approaches (radar or bar chart).
paper_title: PSDesigner: Automated Graphic Design with a Human-Like Creative Workflow
paper_authors: Xincheng Shuai, Song Tang, Yutong Huang, Henghui Ding, Dacheng Tao
